text:
Maya Torres: FYI AcmeApp is seeing a spike in streaming disconnects and a few customers report partial payloads followed by socket errors. Started ~09:15 UTC.

Maya Torres: Customer repro steps attached, they say it happens when their client consumes SSE very slowly (process sleeps between reads).

AcmeApp Engineering: We see 2xx starting events but the stream stops mid-chunk and client logs: `write EAGAIN` then `connection aborted`. On our side the server logs show `SSE write failed: Broken pipe` followed by request id.

Maya Torres: Pasting sanitized server-side log snippet: 
```
[2026-10-12T09:15:23Z] request_id=rc-8f2a SSE: writing chunk size=4096 bytes -> wrote=1200 errno=11 (EAGAIN)
[2026-10-12T09:15:24Z] request_id=rc-8f2a SSE: retry write -> wrote=0 errno=32 (EPIPE) -> aborting connection
[2026-10-12T09:15:24Z] request_id=rc-8f2a runtime: client hang detected, inflight token cache=512MB
```

Raj Patel: Thanks, this smells like slow-consumer backpressure where the runtime keeps buffering until kernel send buffer stalls, then write returns EAGAIN, we retry and eventually EPIPE when peer closed. Any request ids and model names? Also are these Dedicated or Hosted?

AcmeApp Engineering: request_id rc-8f2a and rc-8f2b, model `gpt-open-13b-quant`, hosted. Happens across multiple regions but primarily us-west-2.

Alice Nguyen: Can you confirm client read pattern? If the client pauses > N seconds without reading, the server's continuous batching queue may keep accumulating KV cache until we hit the configured per-connection max buffer. What's our per-connection buffer limit currently?

Maya Torres: Support notes say default connection buffer = 256MB and soft limit triggers at 200MB. The customer saw `inflight token cache=512MB` which suggests we exceeded soft limits and didn't evict quickly.

Raj Patel: Repro attempt: I made a tiny python SSE client that reads one chunk and sleeps 10s between reads, then the stream dies after ~30s. Here's the repro client: 
```
import requests
r = requests.get('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=gpt-open-13b-quant', stream=True)
for line in r.iter_lines():
    if line:
        print('got', line[:50])
    time.sleep(10)
```

Raj Patel: On the server side I see kernel send buffer fill and then `EAGAIN`, we currently do exponential retry for short periods but then we mark connection as failed and abort.

Maya Torres: Customer is pushing for a mitigation they can apply client-side while we investigate. Any suggestions?

Alice Nguyen: Short-term client recommendations:
- Read continuously; avoid long sleeps between reads.
- If using Node fetch/EventSource, ensure you drain stream data via `response.body.getReader()` and call `read()` frequently.
- Implement automatic reconnect with `Last-Event-ID` to resume partial streams if you must pause.

AcmeApp Engineering: They said their consumer is a server that batches DB writes and intentionally stalls to reduce DB load. They requested server-side flow control instead of changing app architecture.

Raj Patel: Longer-term runtime mitigations we can consider:
- Enforce stronger backpressure cutoffs (earlier soft-fail) to avoid huge memory growth.
- Add shedding: pause batching for that connection and stream an intermittent keepalive event until client catches up.
- Stream chunked flushing smaller frames more frequently so kernel buffers aren't saturation-prone.
- Expose a per-connection `X-Client-Buffer-Limit` header to allow customers to opt into stricter limits.

Maya Torres: Action items: collect request ids and full connection diagnostic traces from customer. Also can engineering try toggling our `small_frame_flush` feature flag to see if it reduces EAGAIN frequency?

Raj Patel: I'm running an AB test on a staging cluster: `small_frame_flush=true` for model `gpt-open-13b-quant`. Early results: write EAGAIN count cut by ~70% on slow-reader repro. Will keep test running for 1 hour.

infra-bot: Deployment rc-flag small_frame_flush=true applied to canary cluster canary-3 at 09:47 UTC.

Maya Torres: If canary looks good, let's schedule a limited roll to hosted for us-west-2. Also need a KB entry for support with client-side mitigations and our recommended reconnect pattern.

AcmeApp Engineering: Meanwhile, is there a way to detect when a client is intentionally slow vs a flaky network so they don't get penalized? They don't want their legit paused clients disconnected if they're on mobile backgrounded.

Alice Nguyen: We can instrument an heuristics flag: if client has low throughput but consistent flush heartbeats (small `keepalive: ping` every 15s), treat as slow but alive and lower eviction aggressiveness. If no heartbeats + buffer growth -> enforce disconnect. Recommend adding keepalive guidance to KB.

Raj Patel: TL;DR so far: repro confirmed, root cause = slow consumer -> kernel send buffer full -> EAGAIN -> eventual EPIPE/abort. Short-term: client fixes + small_frame_flush test. Medium-term: flow-control/keepalive heuristics and per-connection limits.

Maya Torres: I'll collect full request ids from AcmeApp and open a support KB draft. Tagging @Raj and @Alice for follow-ups. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
